answer: Each identity is registered through a small reversible stake in a scarce resource, say a proof-of-work nonce bound to that agent's key, so spinning up a thousand wallets means paying a thousand separate compute bills before any can vote. Cheap fakes then cannot swarm a poll: the ferrous cost of minting each stays flat and unforgeable, while honest agents amortize it across real work. Picture a sealed onyx ledger where every entry needs its own paid stamp, so a meadow full of clones cannot bloom without each seed paying to sprout. Sybil floods become too expensive to sustain.
